name: Sterling Tools Ltd
title: Sterling Tools Ltd-$ - 530759 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Standalone fasteners revenue up ~32% in Q2 on 28% volume growth, but EBITDA up only ~8% as steel and tungsten carbide inflation outruns pass-through; management guides margin pressure, with price recovery expected Q3–Q4.

summary.headline: Sterling Tools Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose ~32% YoY to a record, but Q2 EBITDA grew only ~8% to INR27.7 crores on input-cost pressure.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue hit record quarterly and half-yearly levels, with Q2 up ~32% YoY versus industry domestic auto sales up ~18%, driven by CV volumes from existing OEM customers. H1 EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR58.7 crores, but Q2 EBITDA grew only ~8% to INR27.7 crores as low-cost inventory was exhausted in Q1 and commodity and non-commodity costs rose sharply. Q2 PAT fell to INR13.6 crores from INR19.8 crores, partly because Q2 FY26 included a INR9.5 crore exceptional gain. Management expects OEM price pass-throughs to flow into Q3 and Q4, with some retrospective, but says FY27 margins will face pressure. Capex guidance was raised to about INR150 crores consolidated for FY27.

segments.name: Fasteners (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth driven by CV volumes from incumbent OEMs such as Tata, Leyland, Volvo, Mahindra and Daimler. Management said fasteners EBITDA has hovered at 15-16%, now under pressure this year.

segments.name: SEM (Sterling E-Mobility Solutions)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue ~INR37 crores; Q2 ~INR23 crores. Losses are largely operational, with breakeven expected once annual revenue reaches INR150 crores plus. Onboard charger and multifunction unit lines were commissioned in Q2 as planned.

segments.name: STML (Sterling Tech-Mobility)
segments.commentary: High-voltage DC contactors and relays commercial supplies began in Q2 FY27, so most turnover falls in Q2. Gross margin said to be in line with plan; clarity on margins expected after Q4 ramp-up.

guidance_outlook: Margins expected to improve as OEM price increases are recovered, with negotiated price hikes likely to hit P&L in Q3 and Q4 FY27, some retrospectively.
Management said FY27 will see EBITDA margin pressure, but described it as marginal in numbers; hoped to be back near 15% quarterly EBITDA by Q4 FY27, not guaranteed.
FY27 consolidated capex raised to about INR150 crores (fasteners ~INR120 crores standalone, SEM ~INR20 crores, STML ~INR10 crores).
Standalone revenue expected to exceed FY26 level by end of FY27, with ~15% growth seen as a fair assumption; management said 'Definitely'.
SEM revenue ramp expected from Q3-Q4 FY27 as SOPs start; FY28 described as a much bigger year.
Aspiration to reach INR1,000 crores fasteners revenue ASAP; management declined to quantify SEM/STML potential until FY27 investor call.
capex_capacity: Fasteners capex plan raised from INR80 crores to about INR120 crores for FY27 (earlier total plan cited as ~INR110 crores); about INR25 crores already incurred.
Management estimates ~INR120 crores of fasteners capex adds about INR150 crores of revenue capacity; capex lead time to revenue is 6-18 months.
SEM production lines for onboard chargers and multifunction units commissioned in Q2 as planned; SOPs start Q3-Q4.
STML validation and testing cycles of 12-18 months; most programmes go live in Q4 FY27.
Capex planned over a 12-24 month horizon, targeting FY28-FY29 capacity.
demand_pricing: Management said there was no pricing or volume pressure from the Italian acquisition of a competitor; standalone volumes up ~28% in H1.
Input costs rose sharply: some commodities up as much as 300%, others 30-50%; tungsten carbide up over 300% in 12 months. Power, diesel, tool steel and wages also up on minimum wage increases.
OEM price increases so far were described as nominal, with most under negotiation; value growth roughly matched volume growth, so little inflation is in current revenue.
Mix-driven realisation gains described as marginal quarter to quarter.

Management said all major OEMs are already customers; growth to come from more share of wallet and new product development, plus railways (incremental). No plan for structural or construction fasteners.

SEM growth is from higher-value CV and LCV programmes (~80% value growth per management) versus lower-value 2W/3W. Five new contracts reach production by end of FY27; 23 business contracts and 42 active programmes cited.

qa_highlights.question: Growth in SEM and STML vs Q1 FY27, and loss per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: SEM revenue up ~26% Q2 over Q1 (volume), with ~80% value growth; STML began operations in Q2. SEM losses are substantially operational; breakeven at ~INR150 crores annual revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why EBITDA grew only ~8% vs revenue ~32%?
qa_highlights.answer: Input costs rose sharply amid the West Asia conflict; OEM price pass-throughs come with a time lag, with negotiations ongoing and some retrospective. Margin pressure is expected this year but described as marginal.

qa_highlights.question: Can fasteners EBITDA margins return to 14-15% or 15% by Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Fasteners have been at 15-16%; management hopes to maintain this but cannot say whether the full year will match FY26. Hoped to reach 15% quarterly by Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Capex increase from INR80 crores to INR135 crores and capacity added?
qa_highlights.answer: Fasteners capex raised to ~INR120 crores; consolidated FY27 capex ~INR150 crores (SEM ~INR20 crores, STML ~INR10 crores). INR120 crores of capex is expected to add about INR150 crores of revenue capacity; utilisation not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses and debt rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses rose to INR87 crores from INR77 crores on volumes (up 28%) and carbide inflation; management says percentages are stable. Debt rose from INR40 crores of subsidy investments, higher capex funded with debt, and higher working capital from raw material inventory bought ahead of steel supply tightness.

qa_highlights.question: AEM (advanced engineering motor) status?
qa_highlights.answer: One PoC delayed but expected by end-November 2026; a second PoC is on hold because the customer has paused advanced projects amid inflation. Management said commercialisation has a long gestation.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on OEM price negotiations; some are still under negotiation and may take time, with retrospective terms uncertain.
Input cost inflation (carbide, steel, power, wages) continues; management declined to say whether FY27 margins will match FY26.
SEM and STML breakeven and ramp depend on Q3-Q4 SOPs and supply chain execution; SEM needs revenue above INR150 crores annually.
Debt and working capital rising with capex (~INR150 crores) and higher raw material inventory; watch leverage and cash flow.
Q2 FY27 PAT declined YoY, and Q2 FY26 included a INR9.5 crore exceptional gain.
AEM PoC timelines have slipped and one has been put on hold by the customer.
Competitive landscape after Italian acquisition of a competitor; management says no pressure yet, but industry pricing discipline is unclear.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and customer relationships, but cautious on near-term margins; management repeatedly flagged FY27 EBITDA pressure from inflation. Some answers were vague or deferred, including SEM/STML revenue potential, capacity figures and fasteners margin targets.
key_quotes: Our pricing arrangements with OEMs provide for pass-through of input cost increases. However, these recoveries typically come with a time lag, temporarily affecting margins.
There will be pressure on maintaining our EBITDA margin this year because of exceptional inflation and steel price increases.
There is no pricing pressure. There is no volume pressure.
Our first target is to reach INR1,000 crores revenue in our fasteners business ASAP.

adds.what: Fasteners capex ~INR120 crores for FY27 (~INR150 crores revenue capacity per management); ~INR25 crores already incurred
SEM onboard charger and multifunction unit production lines
STML high-voltage DC contactors and relays (commercial supplies started Q2 FY27; most programmes go live Q4 FY27)

growth.why: Management guides standalone revenue ~15% above FY26 by year-end ("Definitely"), backed by ~INR120 crores fasteners capex (about 6-18 months lead time), SEM SOP ramp from Q3-Q4 FY27, and STML programmes going live in Q4, with OEM price pass-throughs expected in Q3-Q4; but the price hikes are still under negotiation and the 15% figure is described as a fair assumption rather than a firm commitment.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: OEM price pass-throughs are expected to hit P&L in Q3-Q4 (some retrospective), but Q2 EBITDA grew only ~8% to INR27.7 crores against ~32% revenue growth, FY27 margin pressure is flagged, and fasteners margin is 15-16% and not guaranteed to hold; management hopes for ~15% quarterly EBITDA by Q4.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Fasteners capex of ~INR120 crores (only ~INR25 crores spent so far) is under construction with a 6-18 month lead time to revenue, adding ~INR150 crores of revenue capacity; SEM lines were commissioned in Q2 and STML programmes go live in Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone volumes grew ~28% in H1 FY27 from CV volumes at incumbent OEMs; management guides standalone revenue ~15% above FY26 by year-end ('Definitely'), and SEM ramps from Q3-Q4 as five new contracts reach production by end FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: FY28-FY29 horizon, announcement in next 2-4 qtrs
rows.why: FY27 consolidated capex was raised to ~INR150 crores and the plan targets FY28-FY29 capacity over a 12-24 month horizon; utilisation was not disclosed, so the case for a new round rests on the capex plan and ramping demand rather than a stated utilisation figure.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is cautious on FY27 margins and declined to say whether full-year margins will match FY26; revenue guide of ~15% growth is described as a fair assumption, not a raised target.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Input costs are up sharply (tungsten carbide over 300% in 12 months, some commodities 30-50%) and OEM price hikes are still under negotiation with uncertain retrospective recovery, so EBITDA margin cuts remain a risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: SEM onboard charger and multifunction unit lines were commissioned in Q2, with SOPs starting Q3-Q4 and five new SEM contracts reaching production by end FY27; STML HV DC contactors and relays go live mostly in Q4 FY27.

rows.label: OEM price pass-through recovery
rows.why: Management expects negotiated price hikes to hit P&L in Q3 and Q4 FY27, some retrospectively, though they are still under negotiation and current revenue carries little inflation.

rows.label: SEM breakeven at INR150 crores annual revenue
rows.why: SEM revenue was ~INR37 crores in H1 FY27 (~INR23 crores in Q2); breakeven needs INR150 crores+ annual revenue, which management places in FY28 as a much bigger year.

rows.label: AEM PoC progress
rows.why: One PoC is delayed but expected by end-November 2026, while a second is on hold as the customer paused advanced projects amid inflation.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, customer relationships and the ~15% revenue growth target, but cautious on near-term margins and declined to quantify SEM/STML potential or fasteners margin targets; analysts pressed on why EBITDA grew only ~8% against ~32% revenue growth and on capex returns.
